gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies a Gaussian-kernel convolution bandwidth and normalization error. It does not identify the separate Monte Carlo coefficient convention and resulting N-dependent regularization penalty.

ISSUE-006 concerns an unsupported relative quadrature/generalization inequality, whereas the gold issue concerns nonexistence of empirical minimizers caused by potentially negative collocation weights. The prediction does not recognize the missing nonnegativity hypothesis or the resulting unbounded objective.

Both entries identify that finite atomic empirical measures supported on the countable set of collocation nodes cannot converge setwise to an atomless target measure. Both recognize the resulting failure of the intended convergence argument and propose weak convergence with appropriate residual control.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The setwise convergence assumption is incompatible with finite-grid Dirac quadratures approximating an atomless measure, so the stated convergence and downstream error/generalization chain does not cover the intended regime.

component_coverage.gold_component: Setwise convergence of finite empirical Dirac measures to an atomless target is impossible, undermining the intended grid-based convergence chain.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the same countable-support contradiction for finite Dirac quadratures versus an atomless measure, identifies the vacuity for the intended experiments, and supplies weak-convergence-based repair details.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the false uniform multiplicative comparison between empirical and population losses caused by a nontrivial finite-collocation evaluation kernel. ISSUE-006 uses a different explicit kernel construction, but it diagnoses the same failed relative-bound obligation and gives the same additive-error repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Finite collocation does not support a uniform relative loss equivalence on the bounded function class: nonzero residuals can vanish at every collocation point while retaining positive population loss. The multiplicative lemma and dependent error argument must be replaced by a uniform additive quadrature estimate.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed relative generalization bound fails because finite evaluations have a nonzero kernel, and an additive uniform quadrature estimate is required instead.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly constructs a nonzero finite-collocation kernel element with zero empirical loss and positive population loss, rejects the uniform multiplicative inequality, identifies the dependent theorem failure, and proposes the required additive replacement.
